title: A unified tight-binding description of the electronic structure and Ising protection of superconductivity in misfit layered compounds
authors: G. A. Bobkov, I. A. Shvets, I. V. Bobkova
abstract: Misfit layered compounds (MLCs) offer a unique bulk platform for realizing exotic quantum states typically associated with two-dimensional transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDs), most notably Ising-protected superconductivity. Yet a theoretical description capturing their electronic structure beyond the simplistic picture of electronically isolated TMD layers has been lacking. Here, we develop a unified tight-binding model for metal dichalcogenide-based MLCs, parameterized by extensive density-functional theory (DFT) calculations across multiple structural configurations and chemical compositions. We show that the intervening tetragonal layers play an active role beyond charge reservoirs: they mediate a significant interlayer spin-orbit coupling entirely absent in the standard rigid-band picture. This emergent interlayer spin-orbit coupling is essential for reproducing the DFT band structure of bulk MLCs and, when incorporated into Bogoliubov--de Gennes calculations, provides a microscopic mechanism for the Ising protection of superconductivity by strongly enhancing the in-plane critical field. Our framework establishes MLCs as a distinct class of three-dimensional materials with intrinsically coupled layers and emergent spin-orbit phenomena.
summary: This work develops a unified tight-binding model for misfit layered compounds (MLCs) to accurately describe their electronic structure. By incorporating an emergent interlayer spin-orbit coupling—a feature missed by simpler models—the theory successfully explains the mechanism behind Ising-protected superconductivity, establishing MLCs as intrinsically coupled 3D quantum materials.
main_problem: Developing a comprehensive theoretical description for the electronic structure and the mechanism behind Ising-protected superconductivity in misfit layered compounds (MLCs).
main_result: The paper shows that intervening tetragonal layers mediate an emergent interlayer spin-orbit coupling, which is crucial for reproducing DFT band structures and microscopically explaining the enhancement of the in-plane critical magnetic field ($H_{c,\parallel}$).
method: A unified tight-binding model is constructed and parameterized using extensive Density-Functional Theory (DFT) calculations. Superconductivity analysis is performed via Bogoliubov–de Gennes equations.
model_or_system: The system is Misfit Layered Compounds (MLCs), treated as intrinsically coupled 3D materials rather than isolated 2D layers. The model incorporates both intralayer and emergent interlayer spin-orbit coupling terms into the Hamiltonian.
key_observables: In-plane critical magnetic field ($H_{c,\parallel}$), electronic band structure, and superconducting gap properties.
important_parameters: Interlayer coupling strength, intrinsic spin-orbit coupling (ISOC) parameters ($\alpha(p)$), and the chemical/structural details of the intervening layers.
main_assumptions: The standard assumption that the intervening layers electronically isolate each TMD layer is incorrect; the model captures physics beyond this 'rigid-band' picture.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates atomic structures for different MLC configurations (e.g., $1	ext{H}$-TMD monolayer, $2	ext{H}$-TMD bilayer) and the coupling mechanism via tetragonal layers. Figure 2 compares band structures for $2	ext{H}$ vs. hypothetical $1	ext{H}+1	ext{H}$ bilayers.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical problem in MLCs, develops a unified tight-binding Hamiltonian incorporating interlayer SOC derived from DFT, analyzes how this coupling affects band structure (comparing different stacking symmetries), and finally applies the model to superconductivity via Bogoliubov–de Gennes calculations to explain Ising protection.
why_interesting: The concept of emergent long-range coupling mediated by an intervening material layer is highly relevant for understanding heterostructures, interfaces in quantum materials, and engineering superconducting properties through structural design.

The inset shows the hexagonal Brillouin zone with the high-symmetry points Γ, M, and K. (b) Monolayer parameters ζ1H(p) and α(p) extracted from the spectrum in (a). (c) Bi- layer 2H-NbSe2: DFT band structure. (d) Intralayer disper- sion ζ2H(p) and interlayer hopping v2H(p) extracted from (c). (e) Bilayer 1H+1H (AA-stacked) NbSe2: DFT band struc- ture. (f) Intralayer dispersion ζ1H+1H(p), interlayer coupling v1H+1H(p), and spin-orbit splittings of the upper and lower branches α(p) ± ν1H+1H(p) extracted from (e).

FIG. 4. Atomic structures (side view, along commensurate b direction) of the three MLC configurations studied in Sec. IV: (a) a misfit slab composed of two trigonal NbSe2 layers sep- arated by an intervening tetragonal MSe layer (1H1T-slab); (b) a 1H1T bulk MLC (MSe)1.14NbSe2 in which all trigo- nal blocks share the same stacking orientation, so that the unit cell contains a single trigonal layer (1H1T-I); (c) a 1H1T bulk MLC (MSe)1.14NbSe2 in which the unit cell contains two NbSe2 layers arranged in the alternating stacking configura- tion characteristic of a 2H-NbSe2 bilayer (1H1T-II). The unit cells are indicated by black rectangles.
